Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\alpha>0$, let
$\mathfrak h$ be the transverse space and $H_f=\bigoplus_nT_n$ the free
transverse Fock Hamiltonian of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]],
and let $A_\pm(g)$, $g\in\mathfrak h$, be the maximal creation and annihilation
operators on $F(\mathfrak h)$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]]. Fix a cutoff
$\Lambda>0$ and vectors $g_1,\dots,g_J\in\mathfrak h$ ($J\ge1$) with
$$\operatorname{supp}g_j\subseteq\{k:\ 0<\varepsilon(k)\le\Lambda\}\quad\text{and}\quad \frac{g_j}{\sqrt\varepsilon}\in\mathfrak h,\qquad \varepsilon(k)=\alpha|k|,$$
and define the symmetric operator
$$\phi(g):=A_-(g)+A_+(g),\qquad D(\phi(g)):=D(H_f).$$
Let $d\ge1$, let $H_a$ be a Hermitian $d\times d$ matrix, and let
$D_1,\dots,D_J$ be Hermitian $d\times d$ matrices with operator norms
$\|D_j\|$ ([[def-operator-norm]]). Then:

(a) for every $\Psi\in D(H_f)$,
$$\|A_-(g)\Psi\|^2\le\Bigl\|\frac g{\sqrt\varepsilon}\Bigr\|^2\langle H_f\Psi,\Psi\rangle,\qquad \|A_+(g)\Psi\|^2=\|A_-(g)\Psi\|^2+\|g\|^2\|\Psi\|^2;$$
in particular $\Psi\in D(A_+(g))\cap D(A_-(g))$ and for every $\eta>0$ there is
a finite $C_\eta$ with
$$\|\phi(g)\Psi\|\le\eta\|H_f\Psi\|+C_\eta\|\Psi\| ;$$

(b) $\phi(g)$ is symmetric on $D(H_f)$ and has $H_f$-bound zero
([[def-relative-boundedness-with-respect-to-an-operator]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]);

(c) the free part $H_0:=H_a\otimes I+I\otimes H_f$ with domain
$C^d\otimes D(H_f)$ is self-adjoint on $\mathbb C^d\otimes F(\mathfrak h)$
([[def-hilbert-space]]); for every $\eta_0\in\mathbb R$ the operator
$$H:=H_0+\eta_0\sum_{j=1}^JD_j\otimes\phi(g_j),\qquad D(H):=C^d\otimes D(H_f),$$
is self-adjoint on $\mathbb C^d\otimes F(\mathfrak h)$ and bounded below
([[thm-kato-rellich]],
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-bounded-fixed-n-operator]] (c)).

The product $D_j\otimes\phi(g_j)$ and the coupling $\eta_0$ carry the dimension
of energy in a physical normalisation; this normalisation is a model choice and
no physical statement about radiation or spontaneous emission is made here.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) with completed tensor powers
$H^{\otimes n}$, symmetric projections $P_+^{(n)}$, contraction maps
$\Psi_f^{(n)}$, Fock space $F(H)$ and core operators $S_\pm(f)$ on the
finite-particle space $F_0$ as in
[[lem-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-creation-contraction-bounds]]. For $f\in H$
define
$$D(A_+(f)):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(H):\ \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}(n+1)\bigl\|P_+^{(n+1)}(f\otimes\psi_n)\bigr\|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad (A_+(f)\psi)_n:=\sqrt n\,P_+^{(n)}(f\otimes\psi_{n-1})\ (n\ge1),\ (A_+(f)\psi)_0:=0,$$
$$D(A_-(f)):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(H):\ \sum_{n\in\mathbb N}(n+1)\bigl\|\Psi_f^{(n)}(\psi_{n+1})\bigr\|^2<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad (A_-(f)\psi)_n:=\sqrt{n+1}\,\Psi_f^{(n)}(\psi_{n+1}).$$
Put $D_1:=\{\psi\in F(H):\sum_n(n+1)\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty\}$. Then:

(a) $A_+(f)$ and $A_-(f)$ are well-defined linear operators on $F(H)$ with the
displayed domains, and they are the closure and the adjoint of the core operator:
$$A_+(f)=\overline{S_+(f)}=S_-(f)^*,\qquad A_-(f)=S_+(f)^*=\overline{S_-(f)}$$
([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]],
[[def-densely-defined-closed-and-closable-operator]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]);

(b) both $A_\pm(f)$ are closed, densely defined and satisfy
$A_+(f)^*=A_-(f)$, $A_-(f)^*=A_+(f)$; in particular $F_0\subseteq D_1\subseteq D(A_\pm(f))$;

(c) for every $\psi\in D_1$, $\|A_+(f)\psi\|\le\|f\|\,\|\psi\|_1$ and
$\|A_-(f)\psi\|\le\|f\|\,\|\psi\|_1$, where
$\|\psi\|_1^2=\sum_n(n+1)\|\psi_n\|^2$;

(d) for every $g\in H$ and $\psi\in D_1$ the identity
$$\|A_+(g)\psi\|^2=\|A_-(g)\psi\|^2+\|g\|^2\|\psi\|^2$$
holds.

No boundedness of $A_\pm(f)$ on $F(H)$, no self-adjointness of $A_\pm(f)$, and
no physical interpretation is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, the Axiom of Dependent Choice and the
Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a parameter $\alpha>0$, define the transverse
subspace
$$\mathfrak h:=\Bigl\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3):\ k\cdot f(k)=0\ \text{for a.e. }k\Bigr\}$$
with the $L^2$ inner product, define the bounded multiplier-valued function
$\Pi(k):=\mathrm{id}-|k|^{-2}kk^{\mathsf T}$ for $k\ne0$ and $\Pi(0):=0$, and let
$M_\Pi$ be multiplication by $\Pi$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]). Write
$\varepsilon(k):=\alpha|k|$ and let $M_\varepsilon$ be multiplication by
$\varepsilon$, with $\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}:=M_\varepsilon|_{\mathfrak h}$.
Let $F(\mathfrak h)$ be the Fock space of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]] with sectors
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$, and for $n\ge1$ define
$$T_n\psi:=\varepsilon_n\psi,\quad \varepsilon_n(k_1,\dots,k_n):=\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha|k_i|,\qquad D(T_n):=\{\psi\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}:\varepsilon_n\psi\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}\},$$
and $T_0:=0$ on $\mathbb C$. Finally put
$$H_f:=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}T_n,\qquad D(H_f):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(\mathfrak h):\ \psi_n\in D(T_n)\text{ for every }n,\ \sum_n\|T_n\psi_n\|^2<\infty\Bigr\}.$$
Then:

(a) $\mathfrak h=\operatorname{ran}M_\Pi$ is a closed separable subspace of
$L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$, invariant under $M_\varepsilon$, and
$\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}$ is a positive self-adjoint operator on
$\mathfrak h$ with $D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})=\{f\in\mathfrak h:\varepsilon f\in\mathfrak h\}$
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]],
[[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]);

(b) each $T_n$ is a positive self-adjoint operator on the Hilbert space
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ with the displayed domain
([[def-hilbert-space]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]],
[[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]);

(c) $H_f$ is self-adjoint and positive with domain $D(H_f)$; it commutes with
every sector projection $\Pi_n$ (i.e. $T_n$ maps its sector into itself);

(d) for every $\beta>0$ the bounded operator $e^{-\beta H_f}$
([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]) is not compact and in particular not trace
class ([[def-compact-linear-operator]], [[def-trace-class-operator]]); more
precisely its restriction to the one-particle sector equals the multiplication
operator $M_{e^{-\beta\varepsilon}}$ on $\mathfrak h$, which is not compact, and
the restriction of a compact operator to a closed invariant subspace is compact.

The identification of $\mathfrak h$, $\varepsilon$ and $H_f$ with physical
transverse photons in a chosen frame is a separate model assumption and is not
asserted here; no thermal interpretation of $e^{-\beta H_f}$ is claimed either.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Adopt the objects and
hypotheses of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-cutoff-dipole-relative-bound]]:
$d\ge1$, Hermitian matrices $H_a,D_1,\dots,D_J$ on $\mathbb C^d$, cutoff
$\Lambda>0$, transverse vectors $g_j$ with
$\operatorname{supp}g_j\subseteq\{0<\varepsilon\le\Lambda\}$ and
$g_j/\sqrt\varepsilon\in\mathfrak h$, coupling $\eta_0\in\mathbb R$,
$$H_0:=H_a\otimes I+I\otimes H_f,\qquad B:=\eta_0\sum_{j=1}^JD_j\otimes\phi(g_j),\qquad H:=H_0+B,$$
all with domain $C^d\otimes D(H_f)$ so that $H_0$ and $H$ are self-adjoint on
that domain. Fix $\hbar>0$, a unit vector $v_a\in\mathbb C^d$ and
$\Psi_0:=v_a\otimes\Omega$, and define the interaction-picture family
$$V(t):=e^{itH_0/\hbar}Be^{-itH_0/\hbar}\qquad(t\in\mathbb R).$$
For $n\ge0$ and $t\ge0$ let
$$\Psi_n(t):=\Bigl(\frac1{i\hbar}\Bigr)^{\!n}\int_{0<t_1<\cdots<t_n<t}V(t_n)\cdots V(t_1)\Psi_0\,dt_1\cdots dt_n$$
(iterated Bochner integral in $C^d\otimes D(H_f)$; $\Psi_0(t):=\Psi_0$). Put
$C:=2\sum_{j=1}^J\|D_j\|\,\|g_j\|/\hbar$ and $C':=C\Lambda$. Then:

(a) for all $n\ge0$ and $t\ge0$,
$$\|\Psi_n(t)\|\le\frac{(|\eta_0|Ct)^n}{\sqrt{n!}};$$

(b) the vectors $\Psi_n(t)$ lie in $C^d\otimes D(H_f)$, the series
$\sum_{n\ge0}\Psi_n(t)$ converges in the graph norm of $H_f$ uniformly for $t$
in compact subsets of $[0,\infty)$, and its sum $\Psi(t)$ satisfies
$$i\hbar\,\partial_t\Psi(t)=V(t)\Psi(t),\qquad \Psi(0)=\Psi_0 ;$$

(c) the Dyson sum solves the actual self-adjoint evolution:
$e^{-itH_0/\hbar}\Psi(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar}\Psi_0$ for every $t\ge0$;

(d) explicit tail bound: for $0\le t\le T$ and $N\ge1$,
$$\Bigl\|e^{-itH/\hbar}\Psi_0-e^{-itH_0/\hbar}\sum_{n=0}^{N-1}\Psi_n(t)\Bigr\|\le\sum_{n\ge N}\frac{(|\eta_0|CT)^n}{\sqrt{n!}} .$$

The convergence is proved for the actual self-adjoint $H$ on the stated domain;
this is not a formal manipulation of divergent series, and no all-time
weak-coupling, Markov or exponential-decay statement is made.

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4
and the identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), the radiation extension
postulate
[[post-nrqm-photons-radiation-extension-and-transverse-mode-assignment]] and
the static finite-level dipole postulate
[[post-nrqm-approximations-static-finite-level-dipole-coupling]], in the state
and outcome readings of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]] and
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], in the radiation
sector vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]] and
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]],
and in the units and dimensions of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice, the choice hypotheses of the cited Fock space
mathematics ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) Finite-level matter factor.** Take the declared charged pair, the
relative-coordinate factor $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, the coordinate
multipliers $Q_{j}$ and the dipole operator components $D_{j}=-q\,Q_{j}$ of
[[post-nrqm-approximations-static-finite-level-dipole-coupling]] clauses
(i)-(ii), with the Coulomb energy operator $H_{\kappa}$ of clause (iv) of that
postulate. Fix, as model data, a declared finite-dimensional subspace
$$W\subseteq D(H_{\kappa})\cap D(Q_{1})\cap D(Q_{2})\cap D(Q_{3}),\qquad \dim W=d<\infty,$$
with a declared orthonormal basis $(w_{1},\dots,w_{d})$ of $W$
([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]),
and read $W$ as $\mathbb C^{d}$ in that basis. The model's **compressed matter
energy** is the Hermitian $d\times d$ matrix
$$H_{a}:=\Pi_{W}H_{\kappa}\big|_{W},$$
read in joules, where $\Pi_{W}$ is the orthogonal projection onto $W$
([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]); the model's **compressed dipole
matrices** are the Hermitian $d\times d$ matrices
$$D^{W}_{j}:=\Pi_{W}D_{j}\big|_{W}\qquad(j=1,2,3),$$
read in $\mathrm{C\,m}$; and the model's **levels** are the pairs $(E,v)$ with
$E\in\mathbb R$ (joules) an eigenvalue of $H_{a}$ and $v\in\mathbb C^{d}$ a
nonzero eigenvector for $E$. A **declared level pair** is an ordered pair
$(a,b)$ of orthonormal eigenvectors $v_{a},v_{b}$ of $H_{a}$; its **transition
energy** is $E_{a}-E_{b}$. The subspace, its basis and its dimension are model
data: they are not derived from the Coulomb model and they replace the
unbounded operators $H_{\kappa},D_{j}$ by their compressions throughout this
pair.

**(c) Radiation factor and cutoff dipole data.** Take the transverse
one-particle space $\mathfrak h$, the bosonic Fock space $F(\mathfrak h)$, the
vacuum $\Omega$, the sector projections $\Pi_{n}$ and the free-field energy
observable $H_{f}=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}T_{n}$ with $\varepsilon(k)=\hbar c|k|$ of
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]]
clauses (b),(d), with the domains and self-adjointness of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]]
and [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]], read in
joules. Fix, as further model data, a **cutoff** $\Lambda>0$ (joules), an
integer $J\ge1$ and vectors $g_{1},\dots,g_{J}\in\mathfrak h$ with
$$\operatorname{supp}g_{j}\subseteq\{k:\ 0<\varepsilon(k)\le\Lambda\},\qquad \frac{g_{j}}{\sqrt\varepsilon}\in\mathfrak h ,$$
For each radiation channel $j=1,\ldots,J$, declare real dimensionless weights $e_{j,i}$ ($i=1,2,3$) and define the Hermitian **channel dipole matrix**
$$D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}:=\sum_{i=1}^3 e_{j,i}D_i^W.$$
These are compressions of the actual real Cartesian dipole combination $\sum_i e_{j,i}D_i$ on $W$, so they have dipole units. This explicitly defines every channel even when $J>3$; the Cartesian case $J=3$, $e_{j,i}=\delta_{ji}$ is included. The weights are declared model data, with no assumed normalization or measured direction. Fix also a real **coupling number** $\eta_0$ declared so that the interaction term
of clause (d) is read in joules. The cutoff and the mode vectors are model
data; no laboratory mode content, no Maxwell field, no mode density and no
value of $\eta_{0}$ is asserted.

**(d) The coupled model.** Write $\phi(g):=A_{-}(g)+A_{+}(g)$ for the maximal
creation-annihilation sum of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-closed-adjoint-sector-domains]] on
$F(\mathfrak h)$. The **declared finite-level cutoff dipole model** is the pair
of the Hilbert space $\mathbb C^{d}\otimes F(\mathfrak h)$
([[def-hilbert-space]]) and the operator
$$H_{\mathrm{LM}}:=H_{a}\otimes I+I\otimes H_{f}+\eta_{0}\sum_{j=1}^{J}D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}\otimes\phi(g_j), \qquad D(H_{\mathrm{LM}}):=\mathbb C^{d}\otimes D(H_{f}).$$
For $d\ge1$, by [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-cutoff-dipole-relative-bound]] clause (c),
read with the Hermitian matrices $H_{a}$, $D_1^{\mathrm{ch}},\dots,D_J^{\mathrm{ch}}$ and the
coupling $\eta_{0}$ (its $d$ is the present $d$), the operator
$H_{\mathrm{LM}}$ is self-adjoint on the displayed domain and bounded below
([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]],
[[def-bounded-linear-operator]]). If $d=0$, both the tensor-product Hilbert space and the displayed domain are $\{0\}$; $H_{\mathrm{LM}}$ is the unique operator on that space. Its adjoint is the same operator, and $\langle H_{\mathrm{LM}}0,0\rangle=0$, so it is self-adjoint and bounded below without invoking the positive-dimensional supplier. This degenerate case has no levels, level pairs or normalized preparations. For $d\ge1$, the model declares $H_{\mathrm{LM}}$ its
**energy observable**, in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], with energies,
mode energies and the coupling read in joules.

**(e) The model's evolution and states.** The model's evolution is the
autonomous unitary family $U(t):=e^{-itH_{\mathrm{LM}}/\hbar}$, $t\in\mathbb R$,
in the reading of clause (iv) of P4 and of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]; for $d\ge1$, a preparation $\rho$ of
the model is a state of $\mathbb C^{d}\otimes F(\mathfrak h)$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], with
$\rho(t):=U(t)\rho U(t)^{*}$, and the outcome law of an assigned sharp
observable $(A,u_{A})$ is the reading of P2
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). No
measurement, no detector, no environment, no external field, no rate and no
record is part of this definition.

**(f) Scope.** Clauses (b)-(e) are adopted model data and readings. They assert
nothing about a laboratory atom, sample, mode content, cutoff or coupling; no
Maxwell equation, source model, back-reaction or propagation is assumed; the
truncation, the cutoff and the mode vectors are not derived; and no
identification of $\eta_{0}$ or of the $g_{j}$ with laboratory quantities is
made. The identification of a physical preparation with a state of this model
is a tested identification with uncertainty under P7. The model contains no
photon detector, no sampling model, no environment beyond the declared
transverse modes, and no rate, decay or linewidth statement.

Let $H$ be a real or complex inner-product space ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]), with inner
product linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second, and
with the induced length $\|v\|=\sqrt{\langle v,v\rangle}$. The definitions below
do not require completeness. When the term *Hilbert basis* is used, $H$ is
additionally assumed complete ([[def-hilbert-space]]).

**Orthonormal indexed family.** Let $I$ be any set. An indexed family
$(e_i)_{i\in I}$ of vectors of $H$ is **orthonormal** when

$$\langle e_i,e_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}:=\begin{cases}1,&i=j,\\0,&i\ne j,\end{cases} \qquad\text{for all } i,j\in I .$$Because $1\ne 0$ in the scalar field, the family contains no zero vector: $\|e_i\|^2=\langle e_i,e_i\rangle=1$, so $\|e_i\|=1$ for every $i$ ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]); and the index map is injective, since $e_i=e_j$ with $i\ne j$ would give $0=\langle e_i,e_j\rangle=1$. Thus an orthonormal family is the same thing as an orthonormal set together with a labelling of it, and in the sequel no choice is hidden in passing between the two descriptions. **Orthonormal set.** A subset $S\subseteq H$ is **orthonormal** when every $s\in S$ has $\|s\|=1$ and $\langle s,t\rangle=0$ for all distinct $s,t\in S$. For such an $S$ the family $(e_s)_{s\in S}$ with $e_s:=s$ is orthonormal in the indexed sense, and the image of an orthonormal indexed family is an orthonormal set. Orthogonal means $\langle s,t\rangle=0$ ([[def-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]). **Independence and unique coefficients.** Let $(e_i)_{i\in I}$ be orthonormal, let $F\subseteq I$ be finite, and let scalars $c_i$ satisfy $\sum_{i\in F}c_ie_i=0$. For each fixed $j\in F$, linearity in the first argument gives$$0=\Bigl\langle \sum_{i\in F}c_ie_i,\;e_j\Bigr\rangle=\sum_{i\in F}c_i\langle e_i,e_j\rangle=c_j ,$$

so every finite subfamily of an orthonormal family is linearly independent. In
particular the coefficients in a finite expansion are unique: if
$\sum_{i\in F}c_ie_i=\sum_{i\in F}d_ie_i$, then applying the computation to
$c-d$ gives $c_i=d_i$ for every $i\in F$.

**Closed linear span and completeness.** The **span** of an indexed family is
the set of all finite linear combinations $\sum_{i\in F}c_ie_i$ with $F\subseteq I$
finite and scalars $c_i$; it is the smallest linear subspace of $H$ containing
every $e_i$ ([[def-linear-subspace]]). Its closure in the induced norm is the
**closed linear span** of the family, the smallest closed linear subspace of $H$
containing every $e_i$. The family is **complete**, or is a **complete
orthonormal system**, when its closed linear span is all of $H$. A
**Hilbert basis**, or **orthonormal basis**, of $H$ is a complete orthonormal
family in $H$.

**The empty family.** The span of the empty family is $\{0\}$, which is already
closed, so the empty family is complete exactly when $H=\{0\}$. Thus the zero
Hilbert space always has a Hilbert basis, namely the empty one.

**Not a Hamel basis, and no order is assumed.** A Hilbert basis is a basis only
in the sense of closed linear span: for an infinite-dimensional $H$ the vectors
of $H$ are in general **not** finite linear combinations of a Hilbert basis, and
the expansion of an arbitrary vector is a norm limit of finite partial sums, not
a finite sum. No enumeration, ordering or countability of the index set is part
of the definition; the partial sums are indexed by the finite subsets of $I$,
ordered by inclusion, and that is the convention used on this page.

**Coefficient notation.** For orthonormal $(e_i)_{i\in I}$ and $x\in H$ the
scalars $\langle x,e_i\rangle$ are the **coefficients** of $x$ with respect to
the family. They are well defined for every $x$, without any assumption that
the family is complete.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) with completed tensor powers
$H^{\otimes n}$ and symmetric projections $P_+^{(n)}$ as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]], so that
$$F(H)=\Bigl\{\psi=(\psi_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}:\ \psi_n\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)},\ \sum_n\|\psi_n\|^2<\infty\Bigr\}$$
is a Hilbert space. For $n\in\mathbb N$ define
$$\Pi_n:F(H)\to F(H),\qquad \Pi_n\psi:=(0,\dots,0,\psi_n,0,\dots)$$
(the entry $\psi_n$ in coordinate $n$ and $0$ in all other coordinates). Then:

(a) each $\Pi_n$ is a bounded linear operator with
$\|\Pi_n\psi\|=\|\psi_n\|$ and $\|\Pi_n\|\le1$; it satisfies
$\Pi_n^2=\Pi_n$, $\Pi_n^*=\Pi_n$ ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]), and
$\Pi_n$ is the Hilbert orthogonal projection of $F(H)$ onto the closed subspace
$\iota_n(\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)})$ of vectors supported in coordinate $n$
([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]);

(b) $\Pi_n\Pi_m=0$ for $n\ne m$, so the ranges are pairwise orthogonal and
$\|\Pi_n\|=1$ whenever $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}\ne\{0\}$ (which holds for
every $n$ when $H\ne\{0\}$);

(c) for every $\psi\in F(H)$ the series $\sum_{n}\Pi_n\psi$ converges in norm to
$\psi$, the expansion is orthogonal,
$$\psi=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\Pi_n\psi,\qquad \|\psi\|^2=\sum_{n\in\mathbb N}\|\Pi_n\psi\|^2,$$
and the partial sums $\sum_{n\le N}\Pi_n$ converge to the identity in the strong
operator topology, i.e. $\bigl\|\psi-\sum_{n\le N}\Pi_n\psi\bigr\|\to0$ for
every $\psi\in F(H)$ ([[def-dense-top]], [[def-bounded-linear-operator]]);

(d) $\Pi_n=0$ as an operator if and only if
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}=\{0\}$; for $H\ne\{0\}$ no $\Pi_n$ vanishes.

No physical interpretation of the Fock space or of its sectors is asserted.

A **real Hilbert space** is a real inner-product space $H$ ([[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]) whose induced-length metric is complete in the sense of [[def-complete-metric-space]]: every Cauchy sequence in $H$ for the norm $\|v\|=\sqrt{\langle v,v\rangle}$ ([[cor-inner-product-induces-a-norm]]) converges to a point of $H$. A **complex Hilbert space** is a complex inner-product space with the same completeness property, so that a Hilbert space is exactly a real or complex inner-product space that is a Banach space for its induced norm ([[def-banach-space]]).

**The completion convention is the Cauchy-sequence one.**
[[def-banach-space]] defines completeness by convergence of Cauchy sequences, and this page keeps that convention throughout. It is weaker than $\sigma$-completeness — the assertion that every decreasing sequence of nonempty closed subsets with diameters tending to zero has a nonempty intersection. The two agree in ZFC, but Blackadar, Farah and Karagila note that the closest-point theorem on a $\sigma$-complete inner-product space is provable in ZF, whereas the Cauchy-complete form used below consumes the Axiom of Countable Choice; nothing here silently imports the stronger notion.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix $\hbar>0$ and let $\alpha>0$, let
$\mathfrak h=\operatorname{ran}M_{\Pi}\subseteq L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb
C^{3})$ be the transverse space with $\varepsilon(k)=\alpha|k|$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]],
let $\Lambda>0$, let $g_{1},\dots,g_{J}\in\mathfrak h$ ($J\ge1$) satisfy
$$\operatorname{supp}g_{j}\subseteq\{k:\ 0<\varepsilon(k)\le\Lambda\},\qquad \frac{g_{j}}{\sqrt\varepsilon}\in\mathfrak h ,$$
let $\eta_{0}\in\mathbb R$ and let $c_{1},\dots,c_{J}\in\mathbb C$ with
$$M:=\sum_{j=1}^{J}c_{j}g_{j}\in\mathfrak h .$$
Fix $\Delta\in\mathbb R$ and define the finite Borel measure
$$\nu_{b}(B):=\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}\mathbf 1_{B}\bigl(\varepsilon(k)\bigr) \|M(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}\,d^{3}k,\qquad K_{t}(x):=\frac{1}{\hbar^{2}t}\Bigl|\int_{0}^{t}e^{ixs/\hbar}\,ds\Bigr|^{2}\ \ (t>0),$$
and the vector-valued function
$$A_{b}(k,t):=-\frac{i\eta_{0}}{\hbar}M(k)\int_{0}^{t} e^{i(\varepsilon(k)-\Delta)s/\hbar}\,ds\qquad(t\ge0).$$
Clause (a) includes $M=0$ and every real $\eta_0$, including zero. Clauses (b)-(e) concern the normalized law when $M\ne0$; no nonzero assumption on $\eta_0$ is required. Then:

(a) (factorisation) for every $t>0$ and almost every $k\in\mathbb R^{3}$,
$$|A_{b}(k,t)|^{2}=\eta_{0}^{2}\,t\,K_{t}\bigl(\varepsilon(k)-\Delta\bigr) \|M(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2},$$
and consequently
$\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}^{2}=\eta_{0}^{2}t\int_{\mathbb R}
K_{t}(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_{b}(E)$;

(b) (normalisation) if $M\ne0$, then for every $t>0$ the denominator
$\int_{\mathbb R}K_{t}(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_{b}(E)$ is finite and strictly positive,
so
$$P_{t}(B):=\frac{\int_{B}K_{t}(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_{b}(E)} {\int_{\mathbb R}K_{t}(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_{b}(E)}$$
defines a Borel probability measure on $\mathbb R$ with
$P_{t}(\mathbb R\setminus(0,\Lambda])=0$;

(c) (concentration) if $\nu_{b}=J_{b}\lambda$ for some $J_{b}\in
L^{1}(\lambda)$ with $J_{b}=0$ $\lambda$-almost everywhere on
$\mathbb R\setminus(0,\Lambda]$, if $J_{b}$ is continuous at some $\Delta$ with
$0<\Delta<\Lambda$ and $J_{b}(\Delta)>0$, and if $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ is
continuous and bounded, then
$$\lim_{t\to\infty}\int_{\mathbb R}f\,dP_{t}=f(\Delta);$$

(d) (positivity) if $\nu_{b}=J_{b}\lambda$ with $J_{b}\ge0$
$\lambda$-almost everywhere and $J_{b}>0$ $\lambda$-almost everywhere on a
Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ of positive Lebesgue measure, then
$P_{t}(B)>0$ for every $t>0$;

(e) (tail concentration) under the hypotheses of (c), for every $\delta>0$,
$\lim_{t\to\infty}P_{t}\bigl(\{E:|E-\Delta|\ge\delta\}\bigr)=0$.

No dynamics, transition probability, rate, decay or physical identification is
asserted; the lemma computes an explicit kernel, its normalised push-forward
law and that law's limit.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\hbar>0$.

**(a) The golden-rule kernel.** For $t>0$ define
$$K_t(x):=\frac1{\hbar^2t}\Bigl|\int_0^te^{ixs/\hbar}\,ds\Bigr|^2,\qquad x\in\mathbb R .$$
Then $K_t$ is continuous, nonnegative and even, and for $x\ne0$
$$K_t(x)=\frac{4\sin^2\bigl(xt/(2\hbar)\bigr)}{x^2t},\qquad K_t(0)=\frac t{\hbar^2};$$
moreover for every $\delta>0$ and every $x$ with $|x|\ge\delta$,
$$K_t(x)\le\frac4{x^2t}\le\frac4{\delta^2t},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}K_t(x)\,dx=\frac{2\pi}{\hbar}.$$

**(b) Approximate identity.** Let $J\in L^1(\mathbb R)$
([[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]) and let $\Delta\in\mathbb R$.
If the representative $J$ is continuous at $\Delta$
([[def-continuity-real]]), then
$$\lim_{t\to\infty}\int_{\mathbb R}K_t(x)J(\Delta+x)\,dx=\frac{2\pi}{\hbar}J(\Delta)$$
([[def-limits-at-infinity]]).

**(c) First-order emission coefficient.** Adopt the objects and hypotheses of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-cutoff-dipole-relative-bound]]: $\alpha>0$, the
transverse space $\mathfrak h=\operatorname{ran}M_\Pi$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]]
with $\varepsilon(k)=\alpha|k|$, the cutoff $\Lambda>0$, the vectors
$g_1,\dots,g_J\in\mathfrak h$ ($J\ge1$) with
$$\operatorname{supp}g_j\subseteq\{k:\ 0<\varepsilon(k)\le\Lambda\},\qquad \frac{g_j}{\sqrt\varepsilon}\in\mathfrak h,$$
the Hermitian $d\times d$ matrices $H_a,D_1,\dots,D_J$ and the coupling
$\eta_0\in\mathbb R$. Let $v_a,v_b$ be orthonormal eigenvectors of $H_a$ with
$H_av_a=E_av_a$, $H_av_b=E_av_b$, and let $\Delta:=E_a-E_b>0$. Put
$$c_j:=\langle D_jv_a,v_b\rangle\ (\mathbb C^d\text{ inner product}),\qquad M:=\sum_{j=1}^Jc_jg_j\in\mathfrak h,$$
and define the finite Borel measure
$$\nu_b(A):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\mathbf 1_A(\varepsilon(k))\,\|M(k)\|^2\,d^3k, \qquad A\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel},$$
and for $t\ge0$ the amplitude
$$A_b(k,t):=-\frac{i\eta_0}{\hbar}M(k)\int_0^te^{i(\varepsilon(k)-\Delta)s/\hbar}\,ds .$$
Then:

(i) $\nu_b$ is a finite Borel measure on $\mathbb R$ with
$\nu_b(\mathbb R\setminus(0,\Lambda])=0$, and
$$\int_{\mathbb R}f\,d\nu_b=\int_{\mathbb R^3}f(\varepsilon(k))\,\|M(k)\|^2\,d^3k$$
for every Borel $f\ge0$;

(ii) $A_b(\cdot,t)\in\mathfrak h$ for every $t\ge0$, and
for $t>0$,
$$\|A_b(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}^2 =\eta_0^2t\int_{\mathbb R}K_t(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_b(E).$$
At $t=0$ the amplitude is zero, so its squared norm is zero; no $K_0$ is used.

(iii) if $\nu_b=J_b\lambda$ for some $J_b\in L^1(\lambda)$ with $J_b=0$
$\lambda$-a.e. on $\mathbb R\setminus(0,\Lambda]$ and the representative $J_b$
continuous at $\Delta$, then for $0<\Delta<\Lambda$
$$\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac1t\|A_b(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}^2 =\frac{2\pi\eta_0^2}{\hbar}J_b(\Delta);$$
if instead $\Delta>\Lambda$, then the same limit exists and equals $0$. The
boundary case $\Delta=\Lambda$ is not asserted.

*Motivation and scope.* In the cutoff dipole model of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-cutoff-dipole-relative-bound]] the vector
$A_b(\cdot,t)$ is the explicit single-vertex amplitude with the atom passing
from $v_a$ to $v_b$ and one photon emitted; $\|A_b(\cdot,t)\|^2$ is the
corresponding first-order photon coefficient, and (iii) is the golden-rule
limit of that coefficient divided by $t$. This item computes only the limit of
the explicit coefficient, under the stated hypotheses on the spectral density
$J_b$. It asserts no approximation of the exact model evolution, no all-time or
weak-coupling limit, no Markov property and no exact exponential decay, and it
reports no measurement or empirical rate. The parameter $\hbar$, the coupling
$\eta_0$ and the matrices $D_j$ enter as mathematical normalisation data of the
model; their physical identification is a separate assumption.

Adopt as physical assumptions of the framework the following statements about sharp and unsharp real-valued quantities. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The latter is the explicit hypothesis used to obtain the spectral PVM of a general self-adjoint operator from [[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] in clause (ii); consumers invoking this construction inherit it.

**(i) Sharp observables.** An **ideal sharp real-valued quantity** (observable) of a system with state space $H$ is a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]), together with a declared unit in which its real spectral coordinate is read; the unit is part of the assignment, and no numerical value of the coordinate is asserted by the assignment. Symmetry of $A$ on a small domain is not sufficient for self-adjointness, and the domain is a declared part of the observable.

**(ii) Spectral probability.** Let $E_{A}$ be the spectral projection-valued measure of the self-adjoint operator $A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$ and a Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ the **probability of the outcome in $B$** is
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_{A}(B)\bigr),\qquad\text{and for a pure preparation }[\psi]\text{ it is }\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}.$$
By clause (b) of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] the assignment $B\mapsto\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$ is a probability measure on the Borel sets ([[def-probability-measure]], [[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]). It is the general form of the Born rule adopted here.

**(iii) Nature of the outcome law.** The probability law is a measure, not necessarily a density with respect to Lebesgue measure and not necessarily a finite or countable sum of point masses: a self-adjoint operator with continuous spectrum ordinarily has no normalizable eigenvector at a point of its continuous spectrum, so an "exact value" of a continuum quantity is not represented by a normalized state. An ideal point value is an idealization; a real detector reports a finite-resolution outcome, that is, the probability of a declared Borel set $B$ such as a bin, and the recorded-event probability is that of (ii) for the bin, not the value of a density at a point.

**(iv) Unsharp finite outcomes.** Outcomes of a finite-resolution apparatus with finitely many channels are described, when the idealization uses bounded effects, by a finite family $(F_{a})_{a=1}^{p}$ of bounded operators with $0\le F_{a}\le I$ in the quadratic-form order and $\sum_{a}F_{a}=I$ ([[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]), the **outcome probabilities** being $p_{a}=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$. They are normalized for every state space assigned by P1, as shown by the preceding general-H calculation. This unsharp extension is an operational description tied to an apparatus model; it is not obtained from the sharp observable by mathematical manipulation alone, and the effects alone do not determine what happens to the state after the outcome (P3).

**(v) Moments are a separate matter.** Statements about the mean, variance or higher moments of the outcome law require the corresponding integrability of $t\mapsto t^{n}$ against $\mu^{A}_{\rho}$ and are not part of this postulate; where they are used they are stated with their hypotheses. In particular the existence of $\operatorname{tr}(\rho A)$ for an unbounded $A$ is not asserted.

**(vi) Status.** Clauses (i)-(v) are adopted assumptions of the model. They assert nothing about which quantities of a concrete apparatus are sharp, about the physical mechanism producing an outcome or about the completeness of the description; a laboratory record is a classical event whose relation to the model is a tested identification with uncertainty, in the sense of P7.

**(a) Assigned sharp observables.** Adopt the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) for a declared system whose state space is the model's [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]]. An **assigned sharp observable** of the system is a pair $(A,u_A)$ consisting of a densely defined self-adjoint operator $A:D(A)\subset H\to H$ on the assigned Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]], [[def-hilbert-space]]) and a **declared unit** $u_A$ in which the real spectral coordinate of $A$ is read, in the sense of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. The domain $D(A)$ is part of the assignment: symmetry on a smaller domain, or a formal differential expression, does not by itself supply an assigned observable ([[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). Whether a concrete laboratory quantity of a given apparatus is described by a particular pair $(A,u_A)$ is a tested identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 and is not produced by this definition.

**(b) Spectral measure and outcome law.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the cited spectral suppliers. The self-adjoint operator $A$ has a unique spectral projection-valued measure $E_A$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$, with $D(A)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}\,dE_{A,x}<\infty\}$ and $Ax=\int\lambda\,dE_A(\lambda)x$, where $E_{A,x}(B)=\langle E_A(B)x,x\rangle$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). For a preparation $\rho$, that is a state $\rho\in D(H)$ of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]], the **outcome law** of the pair $(A,u_A)$ in the preparation $\rho$ is the assignment
$$\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B):=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\rho\,E_A(B)\bigr)\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the reading of clause (ii) of P2; for the pure preparation $[\psi]$ of a unit vector $\psi$ it is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_A(B)\psi\|^{2}$, which depends only on the ray by [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-state-vectors-and-rays]]. The law is a probability measure on the Borel sets by [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (b), and it is affine in the preparation: for a statistical mixture $\sum_nw_n\rho_n$ one has $\mu^{A}_{\sum_nw_n\rho_n}=\sum_nw_n\mu^{A}_{\rho_n}$ by [[lem-nrqm-observables-outcome-law-affinity-and-trace-norm-continuity]] clause (b).

**(c) Outcome sets and exact values.** A declared finite-resolution outcome of the quantity is a Borel set $B$; its probability in the preparation $\rho$ is $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)$, and a "value in $B$" is read only through this number. The reading of an **exact value** $\lambda$ is the singleton $B=\{\lambda\}$, with probability $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\{\lambda\})$; by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-measure-atoms-and-eigenvalues]] clauses (a) and (b) this number is zero for every preparation unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$, and when $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue it is the total weight of the eigenspace. In particular the model provides no normalizable eigenvector at a non-eigenvalue of $A$, and an exact value of a quantity with no eigenvalues is an idealization outside the assignment, in the sense of clause (iii) of P2.

**(d) Spectral support.** The outcomes of the observable lie in its spectrum: with $\sigma(A)$ the spectrum of [[def-resolvent-and-spectrum-of-a-closed-unbounded-operator]], one has $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B)=\mu^{A}_{\rho}(B\cap\sigma(A))$ and $\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\sigma(A))=1$ for every preparation by [[lem-nrqm-observables-spectral-support-and-outcome-law]] clause (b). This is the precise reading of the statement that the result of a measurement lies in the spectrum of the observable.

**(e) Moments.** The **mean** and the **variance** of the outcome law in a preparation are the numbers $\int\lambda\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ and $\int(\lambda-m)^{2}\,d\mu^{A}_{\rho}(\lambda)$ with $m$ the mean, read in the declared unit $u_A$ and its square respectively; they exist only under the integrability hypotheses of [[lem-nrqm-observables-moments-and-variance]], which also supplies the formulas in terms of $A$ and the state. For a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi\in D(A)$ the mean and the second moment are $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ and $\|A\psi\|^{2}$; membership of $\psi$ in $D(A)$ or in $D(A^{2})$ is a genuine hypothesis and is not asserted for an arbitrary preparation.

**(f) Unsharp finite outcomes are separate.** Clause (iv) of P2 permits a finite family of bounded effects $F_a$ with $0\le F_a\le I$ and $\sum_aF_a=I$ and outcome probabilities $\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_a)$ as an operational description of a finite-resolution apparatus. That extension is tied to an apparatus instrument and is developed, together with state updates, on the measurement-and-instruments page; this definition fixes only the sharp outcome law of clause (b) and makes no claim that every laboratory procedure realizes it.

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) record the readings of P1 and P2 in the vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology used by the later pages of the category. They adopt no physical assumption beyond P1 and P2 and the choice hypotheses of the spectral theorem, assert no dynamics, no joint measurement of several observables, no detector realization and no empirical result, and make no claim that any physical system is exactly described by an assigned pair $(A,u_A)$. The additive additivity, support, atom and moment statements cited are mathematical consequences proved in the cited items; their physical reading is exactly the reading of P2 fixed here.

Adopt the state postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable and probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2) and the ideal conditional-measurement postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-ideal-conditional-measurement]] (P3) for the declared system, whose state space is $D(H)$ for the assigned nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-pure-mixed-states-and-purity]]). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the hypothesis of the cited mathematics. The following vocabulary is used by this page.

**(a) Declared ideal sharp measurement.** A **declared ideal sharp measurement** of the system is a finite or countably infinite family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ of bounded orthogonal projections on $H$ ([[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]) that are **mutually orthogonal**, $P_{a}P_{b}=0$ for $a\ne b$, and whose **strong sum** is the identity,
$$\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}x=x\qquad(x\in H).$$
The index $a$ is the **outcome label** and the family $(P_{a})_{a\in A}$ is the **outcome structure** of the declared measurement; it is part of the declared apparatus model, not a quantity computed from the state. This is clause (i) of P3.

**(b) The Lueders instrument of a declared ideal sharp measurement.** For a preparation $\rho$ the **outcome probabilities** are
$$p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})\ge0,\qquad \sum_{a}p_{a}=1,$$
and for a pure preparation of the unit ray $[\psi]$ they are $p_{a}=\|P_{a}\psi\|^{2}$ (clause (ii) of P3, read with the outcome law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). If $p_{a}>0$ the **conditional state** after the outcome $a$ is the selective Lueders update
$$\rho_{a}:=\frac{P_{a}\rho P_{a}}{p_{a}};$$
it is a state with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}P_{a})=1$ and $P_{a}\rho_{a}P_{a}=\rho_{a}$ ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], clause (iii) of P3). If the outcomes are recorded but not selected, the **discarded-outcome state** is
$$\Phi(\rho):=\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}\rho P_{a},$$
the trace-norm convergent series of [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]]; it is a state with $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\rho_{a}$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)P_{a})=p_{a}$ (clause (iv) of P3).

**(c) Declared ideal filter.** A **declared ideal filter** is a declared ideal sharp measurement with exactly two outcomes $a=1,2$: the filter **passes** the component in the range of $P_{1}$ and **blocks** the component in the range of $P_{2}=I-P_{1}$. Repeated use of the filter in series means the sequential application of the conditional updates of clause (b).

**(d) Declared instrument.** A **declared finite or countable instrument** for an outcome set $A$ consists of a finite or countable family $(M_{a,r})_{\substack{a\in A\\r\in R_{a}}}$ of bounded operators on $H$ with
$$\sum_{a\in A}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r}=I$$
in the strong sense ([[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]]), the **effects**
$$F_{a}:=\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}^{*}M_{a,r},$$
where each subseries converges strongly, independently of its enumeration. An **effect** on general $H$ is a bounded self-adjoint operator $F$ with $0\le\langle Fx,x\rangle\le\|x\|^2$ for all $x\in H$; the **order** $F\le G$ means $\langle(G-F)x,x\rangle\ge0$ for all $x$. Here $\langle F_a x,x\rangle=\sum_r\|M_{a,r}x\|^2\le\|x\|^2$, so $0\le F_a\le I$. In particular the positive partial sums $S_N$ of any subseries are contractions and have convergent quadratic forms; for a positive tail $D=S_N-S_m$, the positive-form Cauchy-Schwarz inequality gives $\|Dx\|^2\le\langle Dx,x\rangle$, so $S_Nx$ is Cauchy and its limit defines $F_a$. The **outcome probabilities** are $p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho F_{a})$ of clause (iv) of P2, the **conditional updates**
$$\rho\longmapsto\frac{1}{p_{a}}\sum_{r\in R_{a}}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}\qquad(p_{a}>0),$$
and the **discarded-outcome map** $\rho\mapsto\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}\rho M_{a,r}^{*}$. The family $(M_{a,r})$, called the **Kraus family** of the instrument, is part of the declared apparatus model. The effects $(F_{a})$ alone do not determine the conditional updates: distinct normalized Kraus families can share the same effects while defining different updates ([[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]] clause (d); clause (v) of P3). More generally, on a specified measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$, a **declared abstract instrument** is a map $J:\Sigma\to\mathcal B(\mathcal S_{1}(H))$ into bounded complex-linear maps of trace-class operators satisfying: each $J_B$ is completely positive, meaning every finite matrix amplification preserves positive trace-class block operators; for disjoint $B_n$ with union $B$, $J_B(T)=\sum_nJ_{B_n}(T)$ in trace norm for every trace-class $T$; and $J_X$ preserves trace. Its outcome effect $F_B$ is the unique effect with $\operatorname{tr}(J_B(T))=\operatorname{tr}(TF_B)$, its probability is $p(B)=\operatorname{tr}(J_B(\rho))$, and its conditional state is $J_B(\rho)/p(B)$ only when $p(B)>0$, as established in [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]]. The Kraus case above is a concrete instance on $(A,2^A)$, with $J_B(T)=\sum_{a\in B,r}M_{a,r}TM_{a,r}^*$ in trace norm. This declaration does not assert that every abstract instrument has a Kraus representation or that a laboratory apparatus realizes it.

**(e) Declaration discipline.** A model of an apparatus that is used to predict post-measurement states must declare both an outcome structure (effects) and an update rule; the outcome law of P2 alone does not supply the update, and the update is not a mathematical consequence of the effects. The special case in which the Kraus family consists of the projections $P_{a}$ themselves (with a single $r$ per outcome) is the Lueders instrument of clauses (a)-(b). The claim that a concrete laboratory device realizes a particular declared measurement, filter or instrument is a physical identification with uncertainty under the preparation and apparatus postulate P7 ([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), not a consequence of this definition.

**(f) Limits.** Declared ideal sharp measurements are idealizations of apparatus that are idealized as repeatable and projection-valued; the framework does not assert that every apparatus, or any particular apparatus, is of this form (clause (v) of P3). The following are outside the declared class and require their own models: a measurement of an exact value of a quantity whose spectrum is continuous (no normalization of a delta symbol is intended; clauses (iii) of P2 and (v) of P3); a photon-absorption or other destructive detector, whose declared instrument need not leave an outgoing state of the same form (clause (v) of P3); and a unitary system-apparatus interaction, which by itself produces conditional correlations without selecting a unique recorded outcome or a preferred outcome family (clause (v) of P3).

**(g) Status.** Clauses (a)-(f) read P1, P2 and P3 in the measurement vocabulary of this page and fix the terminology of the page's later items; they add no assumption to those postulates. The cited mathematical items ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-finite-effects-and-instruments]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-countable-kraus-normalization]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-general-trace-class-instrument-and-effect-duality]]) are conditional mathematics about the displayed formulas; no physical process, outcome uniqueness or empirical fact is deduced here.

**(a) Dimensions.** Write $\ell$, $\tau$, $\mu$, $\vartheta$ for the four independent dimension symbols of length, duration, mass and electric charge. A **dimension** is an element of $\mathbb Z^{4}$, written $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$; products and inverses of dimensions are componentwise addition and negation, and the dimensionless dimension $\ell^{0}\tau^{0}\mu^{0}\vartheta^{0}$ is abbreviated $1$. The conventions assign to each quantity of the framework a dimension $[X]$, subject to $[XY]=[X][Y]$, $[X/Y]=[X][Y]^{-1}$ and $[dX/du]=[X][u]^{-1}$, with sums meaningful only between quantities of equal dimension, in which case the sum carries that dimension. These are consistency requirements on the conventions, not laws of nature.

**(b) Reference units.** The **metre** (m), **second** (s), **kilogram** (kg) and **coulomb** (C) are the reference units of length, duration, mass and charge; a quantity of dimension $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$ is expressed in the unit $\mathrm m^{a}\mathrm s^{b}\mathrm kg^{c}\mathrm C^{d}$. Coordinates of an inertial frame are read with the time coordinate $t$ in seconds, $[t]=\tau$, and the spatial coordinates $x_{i}$ in metres, $[x_{i}]=\ell$; slice distances of the arena are read in metres.

**(c) Defining constants of the current SI.** The framework keeps $\hbar$ explicit. In the current SI the constants $h$, $c$ and $e$ are exact defining constants, with the values $h=6{,}626\,070\,15\times10^{-34}$ J s, $c=2{,}99792458\times10^{8}$ m s$^{-1}$ and $e=1{,}602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}$ C, and $\hbar:=h/(2\pi)$; the vacuum permeability $\mu_{0}$ is experimentally determined and $\varepsilon_{0}:=(\mu_{0}c^{2})^{-1}$. These are unit-convention statements of the SI, not measurements reported by this framework; $c$ enters the framework only through the separate radiation assumptions adopted on their own pages, not in the nonrelativistic spacetime of [[def-nrqm-framework-newtonian-spacetime]].

**(d) Dimensions and types of the framework's quantities.** The dimension map is fixed on the following quantities.

1. State quantities: a position wave function of a system with $d$ spatial dimensions and $r$ internal components is an almost-everywhere equivalence class in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ with dimension $\ell^{-d/2}$, its norm $\|\psi\|$ is dimensionless, and an abstract normalized state and the density operators of the state postulate are dimensionless.
2. Probability: the outcome probability $\mu(B)$ of the observable postulate is a dimensionless number; a position density $|\psi|^{2}$ has dimension $\ell^{-d}$; a momentum wave function normalized against $\mathrm d^{d}p$ has dimension $(\mu\ell\tau^{-1})^{-d/2}$; an amplitude for a finite outcome is a dimensionless complex number, while an amplitude read against a detector coordinate carries the square-root of the inverse of the detector measure.
3. Frame parameters ([[def-nrqm-framework-galilei-transformations]]): $[b]=\tau$, $[a_{i}]=\ell$, $[v_{i}]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ and $[R_{ij}]=1$.
4. Mechanical quantities: action $[\hbar]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; energy and the Hamiltonian eigenvalues $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$; momentum $\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$; position components $\ell$; angular momentum and spin $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; mass $\mu$; velocity of a free spinless model $\ell\tau^{-1}$; force $\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$; a real potential energy $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$.
5. Probability current: $j$ has dimension $\ell^{1-d}\tau^{-1}$; it is a probability flux, not a charge flux.
6. Electric quantities of the model parameters: charge has dimension $\vartheta$; a magnetic moment has dimension $\ell^{2}\vartheta\tau^{-1}$, equivalently $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m^{2}=\mathrm J\,\mathrm T^{-1}$, and a gyromagnetic parameter $\gamma$ in the relation $\boldsymbol\mu=\gamma\mathbf S$ has dimension $\mu^{-1}\vartheta$, equivalently $\mathrm s^{-1}\mathrm T^{-1}$; these quantities appear only in the model assumptions that introduce them.
7. Statistical quantities: a mean has the dimension of its outcome coordinate, a variance the square of it and a standard deviation it; a mean, variance or higher moment exists only when the corresponding moment of the outcome probability is finite, so a symbolic average is not a number unless that integrability is established. Angles and phases are dimensionless under the radian convention.
8. Quantities of later extension assumptions - radiation frequencies and energies, electric dipole moments, cross sections, temperatures and entropies - are declared with their dimensions and units by the items that introduce those assumptions, under the rules fixed here; they are not part of the present list.

**(e) Conventions only.** No numerical value of any model parameter is fixed by this item: no mass, charge, spin label, potential or measured constant is asserted, and natural-unit shorthand (for example setting $\hbar=1$ or $c=1$) is read as an abbreviation for the corresponding SI-dimensioned statement with the constant restored.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice, the Axiom of Dependent Choice and the
Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix a parameter $\alpha>0$, define the transverse
subspace
$$\mathfrak h:=\Bigl\{f\in L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3):\ k\cdot f(k)=0\ \text{for a.e. }k\Bigr\}$$
with the $L^2$ inner product, define the bounded multiplier-valued function
$\Pi(k):=\mathrm{id}-|k|^{-2}kk^{\mathsf T}$ for $k\ne0$ and $\Pi(0):=0$, and let
$M_\Pi$ be multiplication by $\Pi$ on $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]]). Write
$\varepsilon(k):=\alpha|k|$ and let $M_\varepsilon$ be multiplication by
$\varepsilon$, with $\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}:=M_\varepsilon|_{\mathfrak h}$.
Let $F(\mathfrak h)$ be the Fock space of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]] with sectors
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$, and for $n\ge1$ define
$$T_n\psi:=\varepsilon_n\psi,\quad \varepsilon_n(k_1,\dots,k_n):=\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha|k_i|,\qquad D(T_n):=\{\psi\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}:\varepsilon_n\psi\in\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}\},$$
and $T_0:=0$ on $\mathbb C$. Finally put
$$H_f:=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}T_n,\qquad D(H_f):=\Bigl\{\psi\in F(\mathfrak h):\ \psi_n\in D(T_n)\text{ for every }n,\ \sum_n\|T_n\psi_n\|^2<\infty\Bigr\}.$$
Then:

(a) $\mathfrak h=\operatorname{ran}M_\Pi$ is a closed separable subspace of
$L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$, invariant under $M_\varepsilon$, and
$\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h}$ is a positive self-adjoint operator on
$\mathfrak h$ with $D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})=\{f\in\mathfrak h:\varepsilon f\in\mathfrak h\}$
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]],
[[def-hilbert-orthogonal-projection]]);

(b) each $T_n$ is a positive self-adjoint operator on the Hilbert space
$\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(n)}$ with the displayed domain
([[def-hilbert-space]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]],
[[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]);

(c) $H_f$ is self-adjoint and positive with domain $D(H_f)$; it commutes with
every sector projection $\Pi_n$ (i.e. $T_n$ maps its sector into itself);

(d) for every $\beta>0$ the bounded operator $e^{-\beta H_f}$
([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]) is not compact and in particular not trace
class ([[def-compact-linear-operator]], [[def-trace-class-operator]]); more
precisely its restriction to the one-particle sector equals the multiplication
operator $M_{e^{-\beta\varepsilon}}$ on $\mathfrak h$, which is not compact, and
the restriction of a compact operator to a closed invariant subspace is compact.

The identification of $\mathfrak h$, $\varepsilon$ and $H_f$ with physical
transverse photons in a chosen frame is a separate model assumption and is not
asserted here; no thermal interpretation of $e^{-\beta H_f}$ is claimed either.

Let $X$ and $Y$ be normed spaces over the same scalar field $\mathbb K$, read in
the real case from [[def-norm-and-normed-space]] and in the complex case from
[[rem-real-and-complex-normed-space-convention]]. A linear map
$T:X\to Y$ ([[def-linear-map]]) is a **bounded linear operator** when there is a
real constant $C \ge 0$ such that

$$\|Tx\| \le C\|x\| \qquad \text{for all } x \in X.$$

Any such $C$ is called a **bound** for $T$.

Let $X$ and $Y$ be normed spaces over the same scalar field, and let
$T:X\to Y$ be bounded in the sense of [[def-bounded-linear-operator]]. The
**operator norm** of $T$ is

$$\|T\| := \sup\{\|Tx\| : x \in X,\ \|x\| \le 1\}.$$

The set on the right contains $0$ and every bound $C$ for $T$ bounds it
above. Thus its finite real supremum exists by the proved least-upper-bound
property of the library's real field ([[cor-cauchy-reals-lub-complete]]).
In particular every number strictly below the supremum is exceeded by a
member of this set; otherwise it would be a smaller upper bound. No choice
principle is used for this assertion.

The same number is the least bound of $T$:

$$\|T\| = \inf\{C \ge 0 : \|Tx\| \le C\|x\| \text{ for all } x \in X\}.$$

If $X \ne \{0\}$, positive homogeneity also gives

$$\|T\| = \sup\{\|Tx\| : \|x\| = 1\}.$$

When $X = \{0\}$, the unit sphere is empty and the unit-ball supremum is $0$,
so $\|T\| = 0$.

derivations.claim: [The first Dyson term in the one-photon sector at level $b$] By [F1] and [F2], $\Psi_1(t)=-(i/\hbar)\int_0^tV(s)\Psi_0\,ds$ with $V(s)=e^{isH_0/\hbar}Be^{-isH_0/\hbar}$. The free initial phase is $e^{-isH_0/\hbar}\Psi_0=e^{-isE_a/\hbar}\Psi_0$, and $B\Psi_0=\eta_0\sum_jD_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_a\otimes g_j$. In the linear-first convention, the coefficient of $v_b$ in $e^{isH_a/\hbar}D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_a$ is $\langle e^{isH_a/\hbar}D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_a,v_b\rangle=e^{isE_b/\hbar}c_j$ by [F3]. Consequently $Q_bV(s)\Psi_0=v_b\otimes\eta_0 e^{-is\Delta/\hbar}e^{is\varepsilon/\hbar}M$. The bounded projection passes through the vector integral, giving $Q_b\Psi_1(t)=v_b\otimes[-(i\eta_0/\hbar)\int_0^te^{-is\Delta/\hbar}e^{is\varepsilon/\hbar}M\,ds]=v_b\otimes A_b(\cdot,t)$ by the definition of $A_b$. Equivalently, for every $f\in\mathfrak h$, $\langle\Psi_1(t),v_b\otimes f\rangle=\langle A_b(\cdot,t),f\rangle$, with all coefficients in the linear first slot.

[The coefficient] Clause (a) of [[lem-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-photon-energy-law]] with $t>0$ gives $\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}^{2}=\eta_{0}^{2}t\int K_{t}(E-\Delta)d\nu_{b}(E)$, which is $\gamma_{b}(t)$. This proves (a).

[Absorption mirror] For a unit $g\in\mathfrak h$, the first Dyson term with initial vector $\Phi_0=v_b\otimes g$ is well defined as a norm integral: the free evolution preserves the one-photon sector, and the creation/contraction bounds [F1] bound each vertex uniformly from that sector to the vacuum plus two-photon sectors. The sector maps are bounded and free evolution is strongly continuous, giving a norm-continuous integrand; these sector formulas supply the extension even when $g\notin D(\varepsilon)$. No full Dyson-series assertion for this initial vector is used. Set $h_s=e^{-is\varepsilon/\hbar}g$. The vacuum component of $\phi(g_j)h_s$ is $\langle h_s,g_j\rangle\Omega$ in the linear-first convention. The coefficient of $v_a$ in $e^{isH_a/\hbar}D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_b$ is $e^{isE_a/\hbar}\overline{c_j}$ by [F3]; thus $\langle V(s)\Phi_0,v_a\otimes\Omega\rangle=\eta_0e^{is\Delta/\hbar}\sum_j\overline{c_j}\langle h_s,g_j\rangle=\eta_0e^{is\Delta/\hbar}\overline{\langle M,h_s\rangle}$. Integrating with $-i/\hbar$ in the first slot gives the displayed absorption amplitude. Step 1.1 and unitarity give $\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}=-(i\eta_0/\hbar)\int_0^te^{-is\Delta/\hbar}\langle e^{is\varepsilon/\hbar}M,g\rangle ds=-(i\eta_0/\hbar)\int_0^te^{-is\Delta/\hbar}\langle M,h_s\rangle ds$. Since $\eta_0$ is real, conjugating this scalar integral proves $\alpha_{\mathrm{abs}}=-\overline{\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}}$ and equal moduli, including $t=0$ or $\eta_0=0$. This proves (c) for the full complex couplings.

[Exact projection probability] Since $H_{0}$ commutes with $Q_{b}$ (both are diagonal in the level basis and $\Pi_1$ is the degree-one Fock-sector projection and the free field group preserves every particle-number sector, [F1], [F4]), [F2] gives $Q_{b}e^{-itH_{\mathrm{LM}}/\hbar}\Psi_{0}=Q_{b}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}\Psi(t)=e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}Q_{b}\Psi(t)$, so $\|Q_{b}e^{-itH_{\mathrm{LM}}/\hbar}\Psi_{0}\|=\|Q_{b}\Psi(t)\|$ by unitarity. By [F2], $\|\Psi(t)-(\Psi_{0}+\Psi_{1}(t))\|\le\varepsilon_{2}(t)$, and $Q_{b}\Psi_{0}=0$ because $\Psi_{0}$ has no photons ([F4]), so $\|Q_{b}\Psi(t)-Q_{b}\Psi_{1}(t)\|\le\varepsilon_{2}(t)$. [F6] and step 1.1 then give $$\bigl|p_{b}(t)-\gamma_{b}(t)\bigr|\le\varepsilon_{2}(t)\bigl(2\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}+\varepsilon_{2}(t)\bigr),$$ since $\|Q_{b}\Psi_{1}(t)\|=\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|$ and $\|Q_{b}\Psi(t)\|\le\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|+\varepsilon_{2}(t)$. This proves (b).

[Scope and assembly] Steps 1.1 and 2.1 prove (a), step 3.1 proves (b) and step 2.2 proves (c). Only the model's first-order Dyson terms, one projection probability and the finite interval $[0,T]$ entered; neither a rate, a decay, a linewidth, an environment nor a sampling model was formed, and no laboratory identification was made, which is (d).

citations.quote:
Adopt the model of
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-finite-level-coupled-model]] with its data
$d$, $H_{a}$, $D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}$, $\Lambda$, $g_{j}$, $\eta_{0}$, and a declared upward
level pair $(a,b)$ with transition energy $\Delta=E_{a}-E_{b}>0$ and page
coefficients $c_{j}=\langle D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}v_{a},v_{b}\rangle$, mode vector $M$ and
photon density $\nu_{b}$ of
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-spectral-transition-and-detection]] clauses
(b),(c). Write $H_{0}:=H_{a}\otimes I+I\otimes H_{f}$ and
$B:=\eta_{0}\sum_{j}D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}\otimes\phi(g_{j})$, so that $H_{\mathrm{LM}}=H_{0}+B$
on $\mathbb C^{d}\otimes D(H_{f})$. Assume the Axioms of Countable Choice and
of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix $T>0$,
put
$$C:=\frac{2}{\hbar}\sum_{j=1}^{J}\|D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}\|\,\|g_{j}\|_{\mathfrak h}, \qquad \varepsilon_{2}(t):=\sum_{n\ge2}\frac{(|\eta_{0}|Ct)^{n}}{\sqrt{n!}}\qquad(0\le t\le T),$$
and let $\Psi_{0}:=v_{a}\otimes\Omega$. For $t\ge0$ let $\Psi_{1}(t)$ denote the
first interaction-picture Dyson term of the model with initial vector
$\Psi_{0}$, as in
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-vacuum-emission-dyson-convergence]] clause (b).
Then:

(a) (single-vertex emission vector) the component of $\Psi_{1}(t)$ in the
one-photon sector at level $b$ is
$$v_{b}\otimes A_{b}(\cdot,t),$$
with $A_{b}(\cdot,t)$ the single-vertex emission vector of
[[def-nrqm-light-matter-framework-spectral-transition-and-detection]] clause
(d) and
[[lem-nrqm-light-matter-first-order-photon-energy-law]]; consequently the
single-vertex emission coefficient of the model is
$$\gamma_{b}(t)=\eta_{0}^{2}\,t\int_{\mathbb R}K_{t}(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_{b}(E) \qquad(t>0);$$

(b) (exact model probability up to the Dyson tail) let
$Q_{b}:=|v_{b}\rangle\langle v_{b}|\otimes\Pi_{1}$ and let
$$p_{b}(t):=\|Q_{b}\,e^{-itH_{\mathrm{LM}}/\hbar}\Psi_{0}\|^{2}$$
be the model's probability of the spectral value $1$ of the assigned sharp
observable $(Q_{b},1)$ in the evolved preparation of $\Psi_{0}$ at time $t$
(the reading of P2, [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Then for
$0\le t\le T$,
$$\bigl|p_{b}(t)-\gamma_{b}(t)\bigr|\le \varepsilon_{2}(t)\bigl(2\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}+\varepsilon_{2}(t)\bigr);$$
in particular the exact probability equals the single-vertex coefficient up to
the explicit Dyson tail, which is not asserted to be small;

(c) (absorption mirror) let $g\in\mathfrak h$ be a unit vector, let
$\Psi_1^g(t)$ be the first interaction-picture Dyson term with initial
vector $\Phi_0=v_b\otimes g$, defined as a norm integral using the
finite-photon-sector creation/contraction action, and define the physical
transition amplitudes with the output vector in the first slot,
$$\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}(t):=\langle\Psi_1(t),v_b\otimes g\rangle,\qquad \alpha_{\mathrm{abs}}(t):=\langle\Psi_1^g(t),v_a\otimes\Omega\rangle.$$
Then for every $t\ge0$,
$$\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}(t)=-\frac{i\eta_0}{\hbar}\int_0^te^{-i\Delta s/\hbar}\langle M,e^{-is\varepsilon/\hbar}g\rangle_{\mathfrak h}\,ds,\qquad \alpha_{\mathrm{abs}}(t)=-\frac{i\eta_0}{\hbar}\int_0^te^{+i\Delta s/\hbar}\overline{\langle M,e^{-is\varepsilon/\hbar}g\rangle_{\mathfrak h}}\,ds,$$
and hence
$$\alpha_{\mathrm{abs}}(t)=-\overline{\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}(t)},\qquad |\alpha_{\mathrm{abs}}(t)|=|\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}(t)|.$$
This compares the reverse transitions for the same level pair, the same
unit one-photon vector $g$ and the same real coupling $\eta_0$, retaining
arbitrary complex Hermitian dipole matrices and transverse mode vectors;

(d) (scope) clauses (a)-(c) are statements about the model's first-order Dyson
terms and about one projection probability of the exact model evolution. No
rate, exponential decay, linewidth, environment, sampling model or measurement
record is asserted; the identification of a laboratory preparation with
$\Psi_{0}$ and of a laboratory detector with the observable $Q_{b}$ is a tested
identification with uncertainty under P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]); and no value of
$\eta_{0}$, $D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}$, $g_{j}$ or $\Lambda$ is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix $\hbar>0$ and let $\alpha>0$, let
$\mathfrak h=\operatorname{ran}M_{\Pi}\subseteq L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb
C^{3})$ be the transverse space with $\varepsilon(k)=\alpha|k|$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]],
let $\Lambda>0$, let $g_{1},\dots,g_{J}\in\mathfrak h$ ($J\ge1$) satisfy
$$\operatorname{supp}g_{j}\subseteq\{k:\ 0<\varepsilon(k)\le\Lambda\},\qquad \frac{g_{j}}{\sqrt\varepsilon}\in\mathfrak h ,$$
let $\eta_{0}\in\mathbb R$ and let $c_{1},\dots,c_{J}\in\mathbb C$ with
$$M:=\sum_{j=1}^{J}c_{j}g_{j}\in\mathfrak h .$$
Fix $\Delta\in\mathbb R$ and define the finite Borel measure
$$\nu_{b}(B):=\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}\mathbf 1_{B}\bigl(\varepsilon(k)\bigr) \|M(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2}\,d^{3}k,\qquad K_{t}(x):=\frac{1}{\hbar^{2}t}\Bigl|\int_{0}^{t}e^{ixs/\hbar}\,ds\Bigr|^{2}\ \ (t>0),$$
and the vector-valued function
$$A_{b}(k,t):=-\frac{i\eta_{0}}{\hbar}M(k)\int_{0}^{t} e^{i(\varepsilon(k)-\Delta)s/\hbar}\,ds\qquad(t\ge0).$$
Clause (a) includes $M=0$ and every real $\eta_0$, including zero. Clauses (b)-(e) concern the normalized law when $M\ne0$; no nonzero assumption on $\eta_0$ is required. Then:

(a) (factorisation) for every $t>0$ and almost every $k\in\mathbb R^{3}$,
$$|A_{b}(k,t)|^{2}=\eta_{0}^{2}\,t\,K_{t}\bigl(\varepsilon(k)-\Delta\bigr) \|M(k)\|_{\mathbb C^{3}}^{2},$$
and consequently
$\|A_{b}(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}^{2}=\eta_{0}^{2}t\int_{\mathbb R}
K_{t}(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_{b}(E)$;

(b) (normalisation) if $M\ne0$, then for every $t>0$ the denominator
$\int_{\mathbb R}K_{t}(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_{b}(E)$ is finite and strictly positive,
so
$$P_{t}(B):=\frac{\int_{B}K_{t}(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_{b}(E)} {\int_{\mathbb R}K_{t}(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_{b}(E)}$$
defines a Borel probability measure on $\mathbb R$ with
$P_{t}(\mathbb R\setminus(0,\Lambda])=0$;

(c) (concentration) if $\nu_{b}=J_{b}\lambda$ for some $J_{b}\in
L^{1}(\lambda)$ with $J_{b}=0$ $\lambda$-almost everywhere on
$\mathbb R\setminus(0,\Lambda]$, if $J_{b}$ is continuous at some $\Delta$ with
$0<\Delta<\Lambda$ and $J_{b}(\Delta)>0$, and if $f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb C$ is
continuous and bounded, then
$$\lim_{t\to\infty}\int_{\mathbb R}f\,dP_{t}=f(\Delta);$$

(d) (positivity) if $\nu_{b}=J_{b}\lambda$ with $J_{b}\ge0$
$\lambda$-almost everywhere and $J_{b}>0$ $\lambda$-almost everywhere on a
Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ of positive Lebesgue measure, then
$P_{t}(B)>0$ for every $t>0$;

(e) (tail concentration) under the hypotheses of (c), for every $\delta>0$,
$\lim_{t\to\infty}P_{t}\bigl(\{E:|E-\Delta|\ge\delta\}\bigr)=0$.

No dynamics, transition probability, rate, decay or physical identification is
asserted; the lemma computes an explicit kernel, its normalised push-forward
law and that law's limit.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\hbar>0$.

**(a) The golden-rule kernel.** For $t>0$ define
$$K_t(x):=\frac1{\hbar^2t}\Bigl|\int_0^te^{ixs/\hbar}\,ds\Bigr|^2,\qquad x\in\mathbb R .$$
Then $K_t$ is continuous, nonnegative and even, and for $x\ne0$
$$K_t(x)=\frac{4\sin^2\bigl(xt/(2\hbar)\bigr)}{x^2t},\qquad K_t(0)=\frac t{\hbar^2};$$
moreover for every $\delta>0$ and every $x$ with $|x|\ge\delta$,
$$K_t(x)\le\frac4{x^2t}\le\frac4{\delta^2t},\qquad\text{and}\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}K_t(x)\,dx=\frac{2\pi}{\hbar}.$$

**(b) Approximate identity.** Let $J\in L^1(\mathbb R)$
([[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]) and let $\Delta\in\mathbb R$.
If the representative $J$ is continuous at $\Delta$
([[def-continuity-real]]), then
$$\lim_{t\to\infty}\int_{\mathbb R}K_t(x)J(\Delta+x)\,dx=\frac{2\pi}{\hbar}J(\Delta)$$
([[def-limits-at-infinity]]).

**(c) First-order emission coefficient.** Adopt the objects and hypotheses of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-cutoff-dipole-relative-bound]]: $\alpha>0$, the
transverse space $\mathfrak h=\operatorname{ran}M_\Pi$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]]
with $\varepsilon(k)=\alpha|k|$, the cutoff $\Lambda>0$, the vectors
$g_1,\dots,g_J\in\mathfrak h$ ($J\ge1$) with
$$\operatorname{supp}g_j\subseteq\{k:\ 0<\varepsilon(k)\le\Lambda\},\qquad \frac{g_j}{\sqrt\varepsilon}\in\mathfrak h,$$
the Hermitian $d\times d$ matrices $H_a,D_1,\dots,D_J$ and the coupling
$\eta_0\in\mathbb R$. Let $v_a,v_b$ be orthonormal eigenvectors of $H_a$ with
$H_av_a=E_av_a$, $H_av_b=E_av_b$, and let $\Delta:=E_a-E_b>0$. Put
$$c_j:=\langle D_jv_a,v_b\rangle\ (\mathbb C^d\text{ inner product}),\qquad M:=\sum_{j=1}^Jc_jg_j\in\mathfrak h,$$
and define the finite Borel measure
$$\nu_b(A):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\mathbf 1_A(\varepsilon(k))\,\|M(k)\|^2\,d^3k, \qquad A\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel},$$
and for $t\ge0$ the amplitude
$$A_b(k,t):=-\frac{i\eta_0}{\hbar}M(k)\int_0^te^{i(\varepsilon(k)-\Delta)s/\hbar}\,ds .$$
Then:

(i) $\nu_b$ is a finite Borel measure on $\mathbb R$ with
$\nu_b(\mathbb R\setminus(0,\Lambda])=0$, and
$$\int_{\mathbb R}f\,d\nu_b=\int_{\mathbb R^3}f(\varepsilon(k))\,\|M(k)\|^2\,d^3k$$
for every Borel $f\ge0$;

(ii) $A_b(\cdot,t)\in\mathfrak h$ for every $t\ge0$, and
for $t>0$,
$$\|A_b(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}^2 =\eta_0^2t\int_{\mathbb R}K_t(E-\Delta)\,d\nu_b(E).$$
At $t=0$ the amplitude is zero, so its squared norm is zero; no $K_0$ is used.

(iii) if $\nu_b=J_b\lambda$ for some $J_b\in L^1(\lambda)$ with $J_b=0$
$\lambda$-a.e. on $\mathbb R\setminus(0,\Lambda]$ and the representative $J_b$
continuous at $\Delta$, then for $0<\Delta<\Lambda$
$$\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac1t\|A_b(\cdot,t)\|_{\mathfrak h}^2 =\frac{2\pi\eta_0^2}{\hbar}J_b(\Delta);$$
if instead $\Delta>\Lambda$, then the same limit exists and equals $0$. The
boundary case $\Delta=\Lambda$ is not asserted.

*Motivation and scope.* In the cutoff dipole model of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-cutoff-dipole-relative-bound]] the vector
$A_b(\cdot,t)$ is the explicit single-vertex amplitude with the atom passing
from $v_a$ to $v_b$ and one photon emitted; $\|A_b(\cdot,t)\|^2$ is the
corresponding first-order photon coefficient, and (iii) is the golden-rule
limit of that coefficient divided by $t$. This item computes only the limit of
the explicit coefficient, under the stated hypotheses on the spectral density
$J_b$. It asserts no approximation of the exact model evolution, no all-time or
weak-coupling limit, no Markov property and no exact exponential decay, and it
reports no measurement or empirical rate. The parameter $\hbar$, the coupling
$\eta_0$ and the matrices $D_j$ enter as mathematical normalisation data of the
model; their physical identification is a separate assumption.

**(a) Dimensions.** Write $\ell$, $\tau$, $\mu$, $\vartheta$ for the four independent dimension symbols of length, duration, mass and electric charge. A **dimension** is an element of $\mathbb Z^{4}$, written $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$; products and inverses of dimensions are componentwise addition and negation, and the dimensionless dimension $\ell^{0}\tau^{0}\mu^{0}\vartheta^{0}$ is abbreviated $1$. The conventions assign to each quantity of the framework a dimension $[X]$, subject to $[XY]=[X][Y]$, $[X/Y]=[X][Y]^{-1}$ and $[dX/du]=[X][u]^{-1}$, with sums meaningful only between quantities of equal dimension, in which case the sum carries that dimension. These are consistency requirements on the conventions, not laws of nature.

**(b) Reference units.** The **metre** (m), **second** (s), **kilogram** (kg) and **coulomb** (C) are the reference units of length, duration, mass and charge; a quantity of dimension $\ell^{a}\tau^{b}\mu^{c}\vartheta^{d}$ is expressed in the unit $\mathrm m^{a}\mathrm s^{b}\mathrm kg^{c}\mathrm C^{d}$. Coordinates of an inertial frame are read with the time coordinate $t$ in seconds, $[t]=\tau$, and the spatial coordinates $x_{i}$ in metres, $[x_{i}]=\ell$; slice distances of the arena are read in metres.

**(c) Defining constants of the current SI.** The framework keeps $\hbar$ explicit. In the current SI the constants $h$, $c$ and $e$ are exact defining constants, with the values $h=6{,}626\,070\,15\times10^{-34}$ J s, $c=2{,}99792458\times10^{8}$ m s$^{-1}$ and $e=1{,}602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}$ C, and $\hbar:=h/(2\pi)$; the vacuum permeability $\mu_{0}$ is experimentally determined and $\varepsilon_{0}:=(\mu_{0}c^{2})^{-1}$. These are unit-convention statements of the SI, not measurements reported by this framework; $c$ enters the framework only through the separate radiation assumptions adopted on their own pages, not in the nonrelativistic spacetime of [[def-nrqm-framework-newtonian-spacetime]].

**(d) Dimensions and types of the framework's quantities.** The dimension map is fixed on the following quantities.

1. State quantities: a position wave function of a system with $d$ spatial dimensions and $r$ internal components is an almost-everywhere equivalence class in $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ with dimension $\ell^{-d/2}$, its norm $\|\psi\|$ is dimensionless, and an abstract normalized state and the density operators of the state postulate are dimensionless.
2. Probability: the outcome probability $\mu(B)$ of the observable postulate is a dimensionless number; a position density $|\psi|^{2}$ has dimension $\ell^{-d}$; a momentum wave function normalized against $\mathrm d^{d}p$ has dimension $(\mu\ell\tau^{-1})^{-d/2}$; an amplitude for a finite outcome is a dimensionless complex number, while an amplitude read against a detector coordinate carries the square-root of the inverse of the detector measure.
3. Frame parameters ([[def-nrqm-framework-galilei-transformations]]): $[b]=\tau$, $[a_{i}]=\ell$, $[v_{i}]=\ell\tau^{-1}$ and $[R_{ij}]=1$.
4. Mechanical quantities: action $[\hbar]=\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; energy and the Hamiltonian eigenvalues $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$; momentum $\mu\ell\tau^{-1}$; position components $\ell$; angular momentum and spin $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-1}$; mass $\mu$; velocity of a free spinless model $\ell\tau^{-1}$; force $\mu\ell\tau^{-2}$; a real potential energy $\mu\ell^{2}\tau^{-2}$.
5. Probability current: $j$ has dimension $\ell^{1-d}\tau^{-1}$; it is a probability flux, not a charge flux.
6. Electric quantities of the model parameters: charge has dimension $\vartheta$; a magnetic moment has dimension $\ell^{2}\vartheta\tau^{-1}$, equivalently $\mathrm A\,\mathrm m^{2}=\mathrm J\,\mathrm T^{-1}$, and a gyromagnetic parameter $\gamma$ in the relation $\boldsymbol\mu=\gamma\mathbf S$ has dimension $\mu^{-1}\vartheta$, equivalently $\mathrm s^{-1}\mathrm T^{-1}$; these quantities appear only in the model assumptions that introduce them.
7. Statistical quantities: a mean has the dimension of its outcome coordinate, a variance the square of it and a standard deviation it; a mean, variance or higher moment exists only when the corresponding moment of the outcome probability is finite, so a symbolic average is not a number unless that integrability is established. Angles and phases are dimensionless under the radian convention.
8. Quantities of later extension assumptions - radiation frequencies and energies, electric dipole moments, cross sections, temperatures and entropies - are declared with their dimensions and units by the items that introduce those assumptions, under the rules fixed here; they are not part of the present list.

**(e) Conventions only.** No numerical value of any model parameter is fixed by this item: no mass, charge, spin label, potential or measured constant is asserted, and natural-unit shorthand (for example setting $\hbar=1$ or $c=1$) is read as an abbreviation for the corresponding SI-dimensioned statement with the constant restored.

nonzero eigenvector for $E$. A **declared level pair** is an ordered pair

unbounded operators $H_{\kappa},D_{j}$ by their compressions throughout this

**(c) Radiation factor and cutoff dipole data.** Take the transverse

observable $H_{f}=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}T_{n}$ with $\varepsilon(k)=\hbar c|k|$ of

[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-transverse-continuum-free-fock-hamiltonian]]
and [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-hilbert-direct-sum-construction]], read in

integer $J\ge1$ and vectors $g_{1},\dots,g_{J}\in\mathfrak h$ with
$$\operatorname{supp}g_{j}\subseteq\{k:\ 0<\varepsilon(k)\le\Lambda\},\qquad \frac{g_{j}}{\sqrt\varepsilon}\in\mathfrak h ,$$
For each radiation channel $j=1,\ldots,J$, declare real dimensionless weights $e_{j,i}$ ($i=1,2,3$) and define the Hermitian **channel dipole matrix**
$$D_j^{\mathrm{ch}}:=\sum_{i=1}^3 e_{j,i}D_i^W.$$
These are compressions of the actual real Cartesian dipole combination $\sum_i e_{j,i}D_i$ on $W$, so they have dipole units. This explicitly defines every channel even when $J>3$; the Cartesian case $J=3$, $e_{j,i}=\delta_{ji}$ is included. The weights are declared model data, with no assumed normalization or measured direction. Fix also a real **coupling number** $\eta_0$ declared so that the interaction term
of clause (d) is read in joules. The cutoff and the mode vectors are model
